content.title: About
content.content: Egg white is the clear part of an egg that contains mostly water and proteins. When cooked it becomes firm, white, and easily digestible. Egg white contains virtually no fat and almost no carbohydrates, making it a staple in low‑fat and high‑protein diets.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: One medium egg white provides about 3.6 g of protein and less than 0.1 g of fat.
The white is composed of more than 10 different proteins, with albumin being the most abundant.
Cooked egg white is quickly absorbed, which is why athletes often use it for post‑workout recovery.
Egg white contains no cholesterol, unlike the yolk.
Heating above 62 °C denatures the proteins, creating the firm texture characteristic of boiled egg white.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Egg white supplies a complete protein source with all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A single egg white contains roughly 17 kcal, making it an excellent low‑calorie food.

items.title: No fat or cholesterol
items.content: The absence of fat and cholesterol makes it heart‑friendly.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Small amounts of riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12) are present, contributing to energy metabolism.

items.title: Supports immune function
items.content: Proteins such as lysozyme have antibacterial properties.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg white, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Protein denaturation with overcooking
items.content: Excessive heating can degrade certain bioactive proteins, reducing their nutritional value.

items.title: Nutrient imbalance
items.content: Egg white alone lacks fats, vitamins D and A, and many minerals, so it should be combined with other foods.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked egg white can be eaten on its own, added to salads, omelets, protein shakes, or used in baking to boost protein content without adding fat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked egg white in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions for up to 2 months.
